headline: Nvidia's founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive on Thursday

sections.text: Nvidia said Huang had resigned with immediate effect after a board investigation into reports about his personal conduct, and that finance chief Colette Kress will be interim (temporary) chief executive. The wider market took it fairly calmly: the S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Nasdaq 0.39% to 25,366.09 as rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6%, though the VIX 'fear gauge' rose 6.9% to 18.70 and about three US shares fell for every one that rose. The bigger story was bonds: the US 10-year yield rose to 5.10% from 4.98% on Tuesday as traders bet on more Fed rate rises, and Brent crude jumped 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel after President Trump said the US doesn't need a deal with Iran. In London the FTSE 100 rose 0.25% to 10,863.09 after figures showed the UK economy grew 0.7% in July to September, its fastest in about two years, while the FTSE 250 was flat; the Stoxx 600 (up 0.1%) and DAX (up 0.4%) edged higher, the pound slipped to $1.3239 and gold fell about 2.8% as a stronger dollar and higher yields weighed.

US producer prices (what businesses charge, an early sign of inflation) are due today. Next week brings UK jobs data, US retail sales and Nvidia's results (about 21:20 UK) on Tuesday 17 Nov, then SSE and Severn Trent half-year results and UK inflation on Wednesday 18 Nov; National Grid and Microsoft go ex-dividend on 19 Nov. Further out, the Fed decides on 9 Dec, with futures pricing a quarter-point rise, and the Bank of England and ECB both on 17 Dec.
Revenue, profit and margins: the three numbers in every results headline, with Burberry as the example. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

standfirst: The shares fell as much as 14% before closing 4.3% lower, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.35% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.25% on strong UK growth figures.
